findings.evidence: “Afterwards delete `<gitdir>/commit-work*`” deletes every matching file, not just artifacts created by this run. Combined with fixed scratch filenames, this can overwrite or remove another session's artifacts or pre-existing files.
findings.fix: Create a uniquely named scratch directory under the Git directory for each run, place its temporary index, patches and message there, and clean up only that run-owned directory. Remove the wildcard cleanup instruction.

findings.evidence: The 11-line “Route by intent first” section is predominantly activation: “draft a message” means “reply with the message text only,” and “stage changes” means “stop after the review.” By line count, this occupies roughly a third of the H2 sections, while Workflow and Gotchas supply the mostly expert index-isolation, snapshot-verification and hook-recovery knowledge.
findings.fix: Condense the familiar intent table into a short guard preserving its safety boundaries: drafting and review are read-only, drafting returns only message text, staging stops after step 4, and committing requires approval. Retain the detailed non-obvious index and hook procedures.

findings.evidence: The partial-file branch starts with “`git diff -U1 -- <file> > <gitdir>/commit-work-all.diff`” without distinguishing tracked from untracked files. For an untracked file containing both approved content and local-only content, this produces an empty diff; the subsequent `git apply --cached --check` fails, and the branch supplies no fallback.
findings.fix: Gate the partial-file patch method on the path being tracked. For an untracked path, explicitly stop and ask whether the whole file is approved or request the exact approved new-file content; explain that ordinary git diff omits untracked files rather than proceeding with an empty patch.
